newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran plans to triple petrochem output in 25 years.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans to triple petrochem output in 25 years.

text.p: Iran, the Middle East's second largest producer of petrochemicals, plans to triple its annual output to 30 million tonnes in 25 years, a senior official said in remarks published on Wednesday.

Ahmad Rahgozar, president of the National Petrochemical Company (NPC), told the daily Iran News the plan required investments of $12 billion in hard cash and 36 trillion rials ($20.6 billion) to build 30 large petrochemical plants.
"We do possess the science and technology to undertake the project," Rahgozar said.
The NPC would use the $2 billion it expected to get in the state budget for the next Iranian year and domestic private capital to build eight petrochemical plants, he added.
Rahgozar said petrochemical production in the current Iranian year which ends on March 20, 1997 would reach 10 million tonnes, up from nine million tonnes last year.

Iran is the second largest petrochemical producer in the Middle East after Saudi Arabia. Tehran has set ambitious plans to boost revenue from petrochemicals and gas despite Washington's efforts to choke its oil industry. ($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
